thread:
Kai Lopez: FYI found an odd base64 payload in webhook logs from partner `zephyr` — looks like a wrapped ciphertext but doesn't have Vault transit prefix. Line: `2026-03-21T20:05:03Z webhook id=zz9 payload=Q2lwaGVydGV4dF9wYXJ0X3Nob3J0`

Maya Singh: can we confirm it's not our debug masking? which service emitted it?

Kai Lopez: service=webhook-ingest-2, container=ingest-handler. I grepped other buckets, same token found in two rotated files.

Nikhil Rao: quick checks I'd run: 1) search Vault audit for any transit/decrypt around 20:00Z 2) check KMS-proxy for rewrap/relay attempts 3) check RBAC logs for any unusual token use.

ops-bot: search completed: 2 matches in s3://redwood-logs/webhooks/2026-03-21. No obvious `vault:v*` prefix on the payloads.

vault-bot: vault-audit: no decrypt/unseal calls for `transit/partner` in 19:50..20:20Z. KMS-proxy: 1 request from svc-webhook (10.5.3.12) responded 400 (malformed ciphertext).

Priya Patel: treat as possible leakage of wrapped blobs until we know. Immediate steps: rotate transit key used for partner payloads, lock down any service accounts that wrote logs, and scrub copies in S3. Also enable focused audit forwarding to SIEM for partner tenant.

Maya Singh: agree. I'll draft a minimal RBAC adjustment: deny `create` on `secret/data/partners/zephyr/*` from svc-webhook until we finish. Nikhil, can you stage the change?

Nikhil Rao: I'll apply a temporary policy using our RBAC layer (policy id: tmp/deny-svc-webhook-zephyr). Will deploy in 10m and monitor for errors.

Kai Lopez: I also propose masking at the ingress: add middleware to replace base64-like bodies > 64 chars with "[masked]" before logging. That will avoid future raw captures.

Maya Singh: +1. Opened MR: https://git.internal/mw/ingest/merge_requests/88 with unit tests.

Priya Patel: rotation plan: create new version for `transit/partner-wrap`, then run rewrap for stored ciphertexts. Note: for Vault transit rewrap we use `/v1/transit/rewrap/partner-wrap`. We'll queue in batches and monitor error rates.

Nikhil Rao: started RBAC patch at 20:22Z — changes propagated in 40s. No downstream errors reported.

ops-bot: S3 scrub initiated: matching objects copied to secure-archive and replaced with masked stub. Progress: 60% (expected complete 20:50Z).

Kai Lopez: partner notified via designated channel — asked them to rotate any client-side wrapping keys and to audit their upload flow.

Maya Singh: added SIEM alert: rule to detect base64-like payloads > 64 chars in webhook streams and to create high-priority incident.

Priya Patel: I'll schedule the rewrap job for 21:30Z with concurrency 3; will run a dry-run on 50 objects first. Also collecting CloudTrail, Vault audit, and container logs to s3://redwood-incidents/3791234567/.

Nikhil Rao: dry-run complete — 50 objs dry-processed, 0 rewrap failures. Scheduling full run at 21:30Z.

vault-bot: rewrap started at 21:31Z — 0 errors so far, 278 objects processed.

Kai Lopez: after rewrap, we'll rotate any SA tokens that had access and rotate partner's API keys. We'll keep postmortem brief and blameless.

Maya Singh: thanks team. I'll follow up on Kyverno/ingest masking deployment tomorrow.

Priya Patel: drafting incident writeup now, target: incident timeline + remediation + recommended RBAC guardrails by EOD tomorrow.

Kai Lopez: closing here once scrub + rewrap done and partner confirms client-side rotation. Will update thread. :white_check_mark:
